title: Teluni Product Architecture
html:
Project documentation · Release requirements · Release policies · Foundation technology map

Baseline and accepted architecture directions

Implemented foundation: Node.js/TypeScript ESM, Fastify, PostgreSQL/Prisma infrastructure, TypeBox/OpenAPI and generated TypeScript SDK, React/Vite with TanStack Router/Query, Pino/OpenTelemetry, local validation and CI configuration. Actual product composition is empty. Installed versions are owned by package manifests/lockfile, not this proposal. No running service/library is added by this document. PH-11 policies and accepted ADR-0024/ADR-0025 select Keycloak, server-managed sessions and application-owned scoped access. PH-11 decision selection is completed; all these product capabilities remain unimplemented.

Decided constraints: use Orion's boundaries; keep a modular backend; support tenants from the first product slice; treat clients and uploaded files as untrusted; avoid premature microservices and distributed infrastructure.

Accepted component direction, not implemented: three product components: an administration web panel, the backend, and a native Android TV player. The initial deployment would serve the panel/API and private media over HTTPS, with PostgreSQL and local persistent media storage on one managed host. The player downloads authorized publications and plays locally. This is a logical topology, not deployed infrastructure.

Component Responsibility Trust and persistence boundary
Web panel Companies, branches, members, devices, media, playlists, freeform visual composition, configurable catalogs/field bindings, regional schedules, previews, publication and observed operational state Untrusted client; generated SDK for API access; no server secrets or direct database/storage access
Backend Authorization and tenant isolation, domain rules, metadata, media access, publication/sync, schedules, telemetry, audit; future integrations Owns canonical server state and API contracts; one modular process initially; privileged migrations separate from runtime
Android TV player Pairing, local configuration, staging, integrity checks, scheduling, playback and bounded diagnostic reporting Independently distributed untrusted client with its own revocable identity and durable local state; never direct database access

Kotlin, Android Media3/ExoPlayer, and durable local persistence are accepted architectural directions under ADR-0020. Minimum Android/API level, media profiles, persistence library, background behavior, package distribution, and update channels remain pending. No player directory or build system is created in this stage. A future repository placement should make the Android runtime independent; a conceptual name such as apps/player-android/ is not an existing workspace package. Kotlin must not import TypeScript application internals; HTTP contracts remain interoperable.

Suggested modules and ownership

All names/placements below are proposed, not existing modules. Follow API module, web module, and dependency rules; group by business responsibility rather than one service per entity.

Module Owned meaning and entities Allowed collaboration and phase
organizations Company (tenant), branch, membership, responsible-administrator relationship, scoped standard/custom profiles, expiring grants and company settings Supplies explicit current ownership/membership/capability checks under PH-11 policies; provider/session/assurance verification remains a trusted boundary. First release slice; accepted ADR-0025
devices Device registration, enrollment session, device identity lifecycle, branch assignment and per-device settings Uses organization scope; supplies permitted device/capability information. MVP
media Media metadata, validation lifecycle, storage objects, access and deletion/reference policy Supplies authorized immutable asset descriptors to programming/publication. MVP
programming Playlists/items, schedules, device/group assignments, default assignment, preview and deterministic schedule validation References media and devices by owned contracts; owns scheduling semantics shared with player contract. MVP
publications Immutable publication snapshot/manifest, target desired version and device synchronization acknowledgements Uses validated programming/media/device contracts; never reads another module's tables as a shortcut. MVP
monitoring Last contact, reported app/storage/sync health and sanitized diagnostic records Consumes device-scoped reports; separates observation freshness from playback success. MVP
Audit responsibility Attributable security/publication/lifecycle events across modules Each capability owns event meaning. Decide persistence/integrity/retention and whether a shared audit component is warranted before extraction; no mandatory generic audit package. MVP
layouts Freeform composition/area authoring and its validated versioned representation Initial release requirement FR-10; exact boundary/ownership with programming and player representation remain D-11. No module is implemented
catalog Company-owned typed field definitions, schema versions, records and scoped data/price overrides; reusable product or weekly-agenda configurations FR-11; expose validated versioned data through public capabilities. Physical schema and publication collaboration remain technical review under accepted ADR-0023
campaigns Promotional lifecycle beyond scheduled programming Future Phase 3; expose explicit versioned data dependencies to publication
Commercial access (boundary proposed) Trial/paid/grace validity, contracted screen capacity, quota admission/accounting and attributable manual commercial state Initial-release policy under completed PH-12; PJ-27/D-12 must review explicit collaboration with organizations/devices/media/publications without mixing financial entitlement with identity permission. No engine/schema/provider is selected
Future integration and commercial automation External clients/webhooks, enterprise fleet extensions, payment gateways and automated subscriptions Future Phase 4; basic manual commercial access is already initial scope. Do not introduce a shared catch-all module

Keep domain rules independent of Fastify, Prisma, filesystem, and providers. The composition root may wire module interfaces; cross-module operations must use explicit public application capabilities with no cycles or arbitrary table writes. Existing ApiModule does not automatically provide inter-module authorization or dependency injection. Confirm the narrow composition design when implementing the first collaboration; do not change foundation contracts to match this planning table alone.

Conceptual entities and relationships

This is a domain model for review, not a database schema, migration, wire contract, or generated reference.

Entity Relationship and invariant
Platform Operates customer companies; platform operational authority is distinct from tenant membership
Company Tenant ownership boundary for branches, members, media, programming, devices and publications
Branch Belongs to one company; holds local business timezone/settings and assigned devices
User / membership / profile / grant One stable human identity can hold independent company memberships and additive explicit branch/capability grants; temporary grants expire, suspension denies, and a designated responsible company administrator approves other administrators. Policies are selected; schema/enforcement remain proposed
Device / enrollment session A device belongs to one company and branch after pairing; enrollment is temporary and single-use; reassignment requires safe unlink/clear semantics
Device group Persistent company-owned programming target in the MVP; may span branches of that company within the caller's authorization. Each device belongs to zero or one programming group and follows it unless an explicit individual override replaces its complete programming
Media asset / stored object Tenant-owned metadata points to a validated immutable file version; storage location is not authorization
Playlist / item Company-owned ordered references to eligible media with duration semantics; edits produce draft changes
Screen composition / content area FR-10 requires freeform configuration, independent areas with optional coordinated pages, regional schedules and concurrent video/audio. Portable representation, renderer and supported profiles remain technical work
Catalog definition / field / record / binding FR-11 requires user-defined typed catalogs beyond products, stable/versioned field meaning and authorized data bindings. Product-price and weekly-agenda views are configurations, not a fixed universal product schema
Price override / publication intent Designated monetary semantics permit company base/branch override and automatic publication of affected published bindings; ordinary unrelated drafts stay unpublished. Durable processing and exact price/representation contracts remain D-10/D-11
Schedule / assignment Associates eligible programming with a device or group and local-time rule; all references share tenant and permitted branch scope
Publication / manifest Immutable validated snapshot of programming, assets and interpretation version; references remain resolvable through retention
Device publication state Separates desired, staged, active and last-reported versions per device; acknowledgement is not proof of continuous playback
Device report / audit event Observation belongs to a tenant/device; attributable action evidence has independent integrity and retention requirements
Commercial period / license allocation / usage reservation Conceptual tenant-owned trial/paid/grace boundaries, contracted independent outputs, explicit device assignment/replacement and reserved/observed usage; approval is not a payment or production quota result. Concrete schemas/state consistency remain D-12

Initial release requirements: release policies define the owner-approved freeform/hybrid regional behavior and configurable catalogs, including automatic versioned price publication. Acceptance targets define the qualification envelope. ADR-0023 establishes the accepted versioned schema/composition/publication direction alongside accepted ADR-0019. Serialization, renderer, physical storage, exact module collaboration and executable contracts are not selected or implemented by product-policy approval.

Further evolution unless separately approved: richer external-data widgets, managed campaign engines, ERP/POS workflows and AI authoring. Configurable fields, product presets and weekly-agenda views are already initial requirements. Versioned textual layouts and automatic price publication must preserve snapshot consistency rather than mutate live data behind an issued publication. Custom catalogs do not imply arbitrary executable plugins or direct per-customer SQL/schema administration.

Tenant IDs must participate in ownership validation for references and uniqueness. The physical enforcement choice (including compound constraints and possible row-level security) is ADR-0018: shared database/schema, explicit tenant ownership and reference constraints are accepted; concrete constraints and the additional row-level-security evaluation remain design work. IDs supplied by the caller never establish authority.

Publication and integration boundaries

Playback/sync owns publication consistency and recovery. Candidate HTTP operations must follow existing API principles, error contract, API versioning, and delivery policy. No endpoint paths, payload schemas, protocol version numbers, jobs, broker, WebSocket, S3 provider, CDN, or Kotlin client generator are selected here. Polling/reconciliation is a candidate; notification transport remains D-04.

Future: an externally consumable documented API should allow authorized partners to update product/price data from ERP/POS systems, with stable generated OpenAPI documentation, scoped machine identities, rate limits, versioning, and safe retry/webhook semantics. Documentation must be usable by partner companies without private repository access. The current internal living portal is not proof of a public integration service. Integrations must pass application authorization and validation; no direct ERP database coupling.

Pending decisions

This table owns unresolved technical design/verification questions. PH-11 owner policies and ADR-0018–ADR-0021/ADR-0023–ADR-0025 are accepted as of 2026-10-18; D-02 retains actual provider/session integration qualification under PJ-24. Acceptance does not complete any detailed design or implementation check. PH-09 has completed business-policy/target selection, with provenance in the release policies; it does not accept technical ADRs or supply hardware/operations evidence. No item is accepted merely because it has an ID.

ID Pending question / candidate direction Evidence required before dependent work
D-01 Tenant persistence isolation, constraints, module ownership and administrative scope; ADR-0018 accepted. The tenant data design proposes composite tenant keys, per-request access resolution, adapter rules, the row-level-security evaluation (not adopted for the first slice, with reevaluation triggers) and the two-company verification suite Owner review of the proposed design (PH-20) before the first product migration; then adversarial cross-tenant/reference tests and the structural catalog test against migrated PostgreSQL in PJ-03
D-02 Qualify Keycloak, immutable claim mapping, server-managed session/assurance integration and application-owned scoped profiles; accepted ADR-0024/ADR-0025. The identity and session design proposes the Keycloak realm/client contract, application-owned principal provisioning, PostgreSQL-backed sessions in an API identity module, the request session boundary, step-up assurance, CSRF/cookie controls and back-channel logout All 38 owner policy answers and the matrix are selected in identity/access. The provider source assessment supports completed PH-11 decisions. Owner review of the proposed design (PH-20) precedes PJ-24; concrete version/claim/session qualification remains PJ-24; external setup PH-15–PH-17. Preserve accepted ADR-0012; no bespoke authentication
D-03 Established credential/pairing mechanisms, revocation enforcement, trusted offline time and verifiable cleanup Implement/verify selected AT-15/AT-16 and unlink/reassignment policies, threat model and PH-08 lifecycle cases; no unanswered PH-09 offline-duration choice
D-04 Manifest serialization/integrity, sync transport, durable atomic activation and protocol compatibility implementation; ADR-0019 accepted Contract examples and failure/compatibility tests against AT-26; latest-authorized-compatible reconciliation and required schedule history. No push infrastructure is selected
D-05 Exact allowed media/codec/rendition profiles, parser/processing isolation and reference-safe garbage collection Enforce selected ingestion/retention limits; PH-08 codec/memory/storage and file-abuse tests before support claims. Tool/provider choices remain unselected
D-06 Shared scheduling fixtures, timezone representation and regional/page state-machine implementation Product calendar/conflict/coordination semantics are decided in release policies; verify date/DST/page/override/no-match and boundary cases rather than silently selecting different behavior
D-07 Android runtime/persistence, supported devices/orientations, restart/startup, packaging and updates; ADR-0020 accepted PH-08 hardware list, unattended operation and power-cut tests; controlled installation and rollback design
D-08 Host/network exposure, HTTPS/proxy, storage, backups, restore/migration; ADR-0021 accepted PH-10 inspection and recovery rehearsal; budget/availability targets; no presumed tunnel/provider guarantees
D-09 Audit persistence/integrity, telemetry enforcement, alerts and scoped support mechanisms Apply selected AT-20/AT-24 report/freshness defaults; audit/legal retention remains PH-13. Review volume, access and observability evidence; do not infer alert channels or remote shell
D-10 Locale precedence, exact numeric/money representation and field/timezone library contracts Business timezone/DST/price override rules and AT-16 are selected; implementation needs cross-locale/timezone/money fixtures. No conversion service or library selected
D-11 Versioned catalog/layout schemas, physical storage, editor/renderer and durable price-publication collaboration Apply accepted ADR-0023 with ADR-0019, implement FR-10/FR-11 policies and qualify AT-04 plus schema evolution, offline recovery and import security; PH-08/PJ-07 remain open
D-12 Concrete commercial-period/license/quota/payment-state ownership, concurrency/reservations and integration with existing authorization/publication boundaries Apply selected commercial policies and CP-01–CP-12; qualify finite quotas/host demand before offers under PH-18 and fiscal process PH-19. PJ-27 must review schema/contracts, state transitions, money/calendar rules and significant mechanism choices through the ADR process; no engine/provider selected

The technology map routes to these accepted Teluni directions separately from inherited foundation decisions. Review/accept significant choices through ADR authoring, then update the owning product specification before implementing them.
